title: Microsoft Purview: auto-expanding archive limit rises from 1.5 TB to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes
summary: The briefing accurately reports the automatic increase to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes, the licensing conditions and the PowerShell controls. It also distinguishes the updated Microsoft notice and Learn banners from the older 1.5 TB body text. No corrections are required.

claims.claim: Eligible Exchange Online archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can grow from the previous 1.5 TB ceiling to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.
claims.quote: Eligible archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can automatically expand beyond the current 1.5 TB limit up to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the previous supported expansion limit as 1.5 TB.
claims.quote: Previously, auto expanding archive mailbox expansion was supported only up to 1.5 TB

claims.claim: The roadmap says mailboxes would become inoperative after reaching the previous 1.5 TB limit.
claims.quote: Previously, auto expanding archive mailbox expansion was supported only up to 1.5 TB, after which mailboxes would become inoperative.

claims.claim: The roadmap attributes expansion beyond 1.5 TB to customers with eligible E5 licences.
claims.quote: This capability to expand archive beyond 1.5 TB will be available to customers with eligible E5 licenses.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters
claims.claim: The increase is on automatically for the eligible, already-enabled archive mailboxes it targets.
claims.quote: No action is required if eligible mailboxes already have auto-expanding archiving enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The increased capacity is included with the named eligible licences rather than separately metered per GB.
claims.quote:
The increase applies to mailboxes assigned the following eligible licenses:

- Office 365 E5, A5, or G5
- Microsoft 365 E5, A5, or G5

If auto-expanding archiving is already enabled, no additional configuration or per-GB charge applies.

claims.claim: Both cited archive articles carry a banner giving the same mid-to-late October 2026 rollout window as the notice.
claims.quote: Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October.

claims.claim: The body of Enable auto-expanding archiving still describes a 1.5 TB maximum despite its updated banner.
claims.quote: When auto-expanding archiving is turned on, additional storage space is automatically added to a user's archive mailbox until it reaches the storage limit of 1.5 TB.

claims.claim: The body of Learn about auto-expanding archiving still describes a 1.5 TB maximum despite its updated banner.
claims.quote: Extra storage space is added until it reaches a maximum size of 1.5 TB.

claims.claim: The increase gives eligible archives additional headroom without a support request.
claims.quote: This enhancement helps organizations retain and manage larger volumes of archived email content without requiring manual archive expansion processes or support requests.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn says no more data is stored in the auto-expanding archive at the 1.5 TB ceiling retained for non-eligible licences.
claims.quote: If a mailbox with an auto-expanding archive reaches a total of 1.5 TB of data stored in the auto-expanding archive, no more data will be stored in the auto-expanding archive or moved from the main archive to the auto-expanding archive.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating internal documentation, retention guidance and help desk materials.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, retention guidance, and help desk materials to reflect the new 3 TB limit.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licence assignments for users with large archive mailboxes.
claims.quote: Review license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licensing and retention strategies for users ineligible for the increase.
claims.quote: Review licensing and retention strategies for users whose archive mailboxes are not eligible for the expanded capacity.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports a mailbox growth rate that does not exceed 1 GB per day.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported only for mailboxes used by individual users or for shared mailboxes with a growth rate that doesn't exceed 1 GB per day.

claims.claim: eDiscovery tools such as Content Search search the additional storage areas of auto-expanded archives.
claims.quote: When you use an eDiscovery tool, such as Content Search, the additional storage areas in an auto-expanded archive are also searched.

claims.claim: Mailbox holds also cover content in an auto-expanded archive.
claims.quote: When you put a mailbox on hold by using methods such as Microsoft 365 retention, eDiscovery case holds, and Litigation Hold in Exchange Online, content located in an auto-expanded archive is also placed on hold.

claims.claim: The documentation describes no new permission or identity introduced by the capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving 3 TB new permissions identity admin center enable specific users. Read MC1472592 and Learn's enable-autoexpanding-archiving and autoexpanding-archiving articles; they give existing enablement roles, not a new identity or permission.

claims.claim: For E5 licences, Learn says to verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled in the user's licence settings.

claims.claim: The cited Learn archive articles state no price for upgrading a user to an eligible licence.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com auto expanding archive 3 TB eligible license removed downgrade archive price. Read enable-autoexpanding-archiving and autoexpanding-archiving in full; both list eligible licences and no per-GB charge, but neither gives licence-upgrade prices.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The user's archive mailbox must already be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Cloud-based archive mailboxes in Exchange hybrid deployments support auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment for users who have an on-premises primary mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving is not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving isn't supported for on-premises mailboxes in any version of Exchange Server.

claims.claim: There is no documented admin-centre UI for enabling organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving 3 TB new permissions identity admin center enable specific users. Opened enable-autoexpanding-archiving: it expressly rules out Exchange admin center and Microsoft Purview portal and gives Set-OrganizationConfig in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: There is no documented admin-centre UI for enabling auto-expanding archiving for specific users.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving 3 TB new permissions identity admin center enable specific users. Opened enable-autoexpanding-archiving: it expressly rules out Exchange admin center and Microsoft Purview portal and gives Enable-Mailbox in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Enabling auto-expanding archiving requires Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving. You must use Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive enables auto-expanding archiving for the organisation.
claims.quote:
To enable auto-expanding archiving for your entire organization, run the following command:

    Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive enables auto-expanding archiving for a specific user.
claims.quote: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.claim: The per-user Enable-Mailbox command requires both primary and archive mailboxes to be cloud-based.
claims.quote: If a user's primary and archive mailboxes are both cloud-based, then you can use the Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command to enable auto-expanding archiving for that specific user.

claims.claim: For an on-premises primary mailbox with a cloud archive, enable auto-expanding archiving with the organisation-wide Set-OrganizationConfig command instead.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment, you have to run the Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive command in Exchange Online PowerShell to enable auto-expanding archiving for the entire organization.

claims.claim: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks the organisation's enablement state.
claims.quote: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks the user's enablement property.
claims.quote: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement does not set AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled to True on individual user mailboxes.
claims.quote: Running the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to enable auto-expanding archiving for your organization doesn't change the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on user mailboxes to True.

claims.claim: Per-user enablement for a mailbox on hold or assigned a retention policy adds 10 GB to the primary archive mailbox quota.
claims.quote:
When you enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user and the user's mailbox in on hold or assigned to a retention policy, the following two configurations changes are made:

- The storage quota for the user's primary archive mailbox is increased by 10 GB (from 100 GB to 110 GB).

claims.claim: Neither enablement control lets administrators choose between the 1.5 TB and 3 TB ceilings.
claims.quote: Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: The cited Learn archive pages do not explain what happens to an archive already over 1.5 TB when its eligible licence is removed.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding" "3 TB" "license" "removed"; auto expanding archive 3 TB eligible license removed downgrade archive price. Read enable-autoexpanding-archiving and autoexpanding-archiving in full; neither explains removing eligibility after growth beyond 1.5 TB.

controlChecks.governs: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation
